result.topic_en: A draft on Riemann's theory of gravitation: matter disappears in ponderable bodies in proportion to their gravity, and the resulting motions of the space-filling substance are determined by boundary conditions, which can be replaced by the requirement that the motions vanish at infinite distance.

methods.what: Law that in ponderable bodies matter disappears at a constant rate proportional to their gravitational mass (sink model of gravitation)
methods.quote:
In [-den ponderabeln-] {+allen schweren+} Körpern ist eine Ursache vorhanden {+welche+} welche
bewirkt daß in fortwährend[?] in gleichen Zeiten gleiche {+ihrer+} [?] ihrer
Schwerkraft proportionale Stoffmengen[?] verschwinden.

methods.what: Uniqueness/determination of the motion in a bounded region given the positions and strengths of the sources and the boundary forces
methods.quote:
Durch dieses Gesetz werden die Bewegungen des Stoffs in jedem
begrenzten Raume völlig bestimmt, wenn die Lage aller ponderabeln
Körper {+in ihm+} und die Größe ihrer Schwerkraft gegeben ist

methods.what: Replacing the boundary condition by a decay condition at infinity (exterior problem approximated by a large bounded domain)
methods.quote:
In diesem Falle werden die Bewegungen des Stoffs in unendlicher

items.english: By this law the motions of the substance in any bounded space are completely determined if the position of all ponderable bodies in it and the magnitude of their gravity are given, and in addition the external forces acting on the points of the boundary are known.

items.quote:
In diesem Falle werden die Bewegungen des Stoffs in unendlicher
Entfernung von den ponderabeln Körpern unendlich klein.
items.english: In this case the motions of the substance become infinitely small at infinite distance from the ponderable bodies.

items.quote:
Wenn daher die ponderabeln Körper in einen Raum [?]
eingeschlossen werden, dessen Begrenzung von denselben überall
sehr weit absteht
items.english: If therefore the ponderable bodies are enclosed in a space whose boundary is everywhere very far from them, and the forces outside it are suitably chosen, motions would result that are very nearly equal to the actual ones (which must be assumed to explain gravity), and they would become exactly equal if the boundary is infinitely far from the ponderable bodies.
